newsitem.title: UK: Medical device company seeks London flotation.
newsitem.headline: Medical device company seeks London flotation.

text.p: New Medical Technology (NMT), a Scotland-based company making safety equipment for medical workers, says it will seek permission to trade on London Stock Exchange's Alternative Investment Market in April.

NMT said in a statement it was developing a range of products including Zero-Stik, a safety syringe designed to retract automatically at the end of its stroke. The idea is to reduce the risk of needlestick injuries, which can pass on infections such as hepatitis and HIV to health workers.
"It is estimated that, in the U.S. alone, there are over one million needlestick injuries," NMT said in a statement.

Its second patented product is Safe Drug Delivery Technology, which will allow pharmaceutical companies to pre-fill syringes with drugs, reducing the need for ampoules and thus the risk of injuries caused in opening them.
"It is intended to raise between 12 and 15 million stg in the flotation, to facilitate automated production and commercialisation of its technology platforms," the statement added.

"The flotation will provide us with a sound financial footing for the future development of the company, in particular allowing us to establish state-of-the-art automated manufacturing facilities in Scotland and a sales and marketing network in western Europe and the USA," said John Campbell, the company's chief executive.
Nominated adviser and broker is Panmure Gordon and Co Ltd. (( -- London Newsroom 44-171-542-8958
